おしい。1/6公式は、2つのグラフの交点で囲まれたときだけ。ここは端が直線 x: Close. The 1/6 formula only works when the region is closed off by the 2 graphs' intersection points. Here the ends are the lines x = p and x = q.
おしい。2人どうしなら差は変わらないが、ここは1人と3人の合計。差は1年に2ずつ: Close. Between 2 people the difference stays the same, but here it's 1 person versus the total of 3. The difference shrinks by 2 in 1 year.
おしい。2人どうしなら差は変わらないが、ここは1人と3人の合計。差は毎年ちぢむ。: Close. Between 2 people the difference doesn't change, but here it's 1 person versus the total of 3. The difference shrinks every year.
おしい。2種類がまざっているが、全部の個数が分からないので、面積図の横の長さが決: Close. 2 kinds are mixed, but you don't know the total count, so the width of the area diagram can't be fixed.
おしい。6×6の表は2個のときだけ。3個では立体になる。: Close. A 6×6 table only works for 2 dice. With 3, it becomes a solid.
おしい。aを止めて求まるのは、すべてのaで通る定点。ここでは点が決まっていて、a: Close. Freezing a gives the fixed point that works for every a. Here the point is given, and you find a.
おしい。てんびんでも解けるが、ここでは人数と点数の長方形で、はみ出しとへこみを比: Close. A balance works too, but here it's easier to see by comparing the bump and the dent with rectangles of students and scores.
おしい。てんびんの重みは時間。行きと帰りで時間がちがうので、まん中ではない。: Close. On the balance, the weight is time. Going and coming back take different times, so it isn't the middle.
おしい。まっすぐにする発想は同じだが、ここでは直線で折り返すのではなく、立体の面: So close. The idea of making it straight is the same, but here you don't reflect across a line — you open up the faces of the solid.
おしい。まっすぐにする発想は同じだが、ここは平面。面を開くのではなく、直線で折り: So close. The idea of making it straight is the same, but this is a flat plane. Don't open up faces — reflect across a line.
おしい。何も混ぜていないので、てんびんの片方におくものがない。: Close. Nothing is being mixed, so there's nothing to put on one side of the balance.
おしい。和は一定だが、まん中は範囲の外。まん中では最大にならない。: Close. The sum is constant, but the middle is outside the range, so the maximum isn't at the middle.
おしい。囲んでも答えは出るが、すみの三角形が4つになる。対角線がy軸の上にあるの: Close. Enclosing does give the answer, but you get 4 corner triangles. The diagonal lies on the y-axis, so splitting into 2 is faster.
おしい。折り返すのは「和」を最小にするとき。ここは「差」を最大にする。: Close! You reflect when you want the smallest "sum." Here you want the largest "difference."
おしい。折り返すのは和の最小のとき。差の最大では折り返さない。: Close! You reflect for the minimum of a sum. For the maximum of a difference, you don't reflect.
おしい。接点のx座標は、Pが動ける範囲の外にある。: Close. The x-coordinate of the point of tangency is outside the range where P can move.
おしい。最短の道だが、PとQは川の反対側。折り返すのではなく、橋の長さの分だけQ: Close! It is a shortest path, but P and Q are on opposite sides of the river. Instead of reflecting, shift Q by the length of the bridge.
おしい。直方体の問題だが、聞いているのは体積。面を開いても体積は出ない。: Close! It's a rectangular prism problem, but it asks for volume. Opening the faces won't give you the volume.
おしい。等積変形が使えるのは、頂点が底辺に平行な直線の上を動くときだけ。ここは平: Close! Equal-Area Slide only works when the vertex moves along a line parallel to the base. Here the lines are not parallel.
おしい。速さの問題だが、動くのは1人だけ。止める相手がいない。: Close! It's a speed problem, but only 1 person moves. There's no one to freeze.
おしい。開くところまでは正しいが、中心角が180°以上なので、両はしを結ぶ直線は: Close! Opening it up is right, but the central angle is 180° or more, so the line joining the two ends sticks out of the sector.
おしい。面積をそろえる相手の三角形がないので、平行に動かす頂点がない。: Close. There is no other triangle to match the area with, so there is no vertex to slide parallel.

そのとおり。1匹あたりの足の数×匹数を長方形で表すと、はみ出した部分だけで答えが: That's right. Show legs on 1 animal × number of animals as rectangles, and the part that sticks out alone gives the answer.
そのとおり。1台あたりのタイヤの数×台数を長方形で表すと、はみ出した部分だけで答: That's right. Show tires per vehicle × number of vehicles as rectangles, and the part sticking out alone gives you the answer.
そのとおり。1回目のてんびんで8%、2回目は8%と0%のてんびん。: That's right. The first balance gives 8%, and the second is a balance of 8% and 0%.
そのとおり。1回目のてんびんで混ぜたあとの濃度、2回目はその濃度と0%のてんびん: That's right. The 1st balance gives the concentration after mixing; the 2nd is a balance between that concentration and 0%.

直線とx軸で囲まれた部分は台形や三角形。積分も1/6公式もいらない。: A region enclosed by a straight line and the x-axis is a trapezoid or a triangle. You need neither integration nor the 1/6 formula.

直線上のPで、AP＋PBの最小は？: For P on a line, what's the minimum of AP＋PB?
直線上の点を通る2点間の最短は、一方の点を直線で折り返し、まっすぐ結ぶ。: For the shortest path between 2 points that passes through a point on a line, reflect one point over the line and join them with a straight line.
相手を止めて見ると、自分は2人の速さの和で近づいて見える（相対速度）。動くものが: If you freeze the other person, you appear to approach at the sum of the 2 speeds (relative speed). With only 1 thing moving, 1 division tells you when they meet.
短針も動くのを忘れて、長針だけで答えてしまう: You forget that the hour hand moves too, and answer using only the minute hand
短針を止めて考えると、長針は1分に 6−0.5 = 5.5 度ずつ近づく: Freeze the hour hand: the minute hand gets 6−0.5 = 5.5 degrees closer every minute
短針を止めて考えると、長針は1分に5.5度ずつ近づく。時計の問題も、追いかける問: Freeze the hour hand: the minute hand gets 5.5 degrees closer every minute. Clock problems are just chase problems.
積の条件は、行ごとに数える: For a product condition, count row by row
立体にもどって考え直すので、約2分半: You have to go back to the solid and rethink, about 2 and a half minutes
立体のままAとGを結ぶと、表面ではなく中を通る線になってしまう。: If you join A and G in the solid as it is, the line goes through the inside, not over the surface.
立体のまま、糸の通る点の位置を文字でおく: Keeping the solid as it is, you use letters for the points the string passes through
立体のままでは、曲面上の長さが計算できない。: As a solid, you can't calculate a length on the curved surface.
立体のままでは比べられない…。どうする？: You can't compare them on the solid as it is… What now?
立体のまま長さを比べたくなる: You want to compare lengths on the solid as it is
立体の図のまま、糸の長さを比べようとするが、ななめの長さが計算できない: You try to compare string lengths on the drawing of the solid, but you can't calculate the slanted lengths
立体の表面の問題ではない。: This isn't a problem about the surface of a solid.
立体の表面をいくつかの面にまたがる最短の道は、通る面を全部開いて、まっすぐ結ぶ。: For the shortest path that crosses several faces of a solid, open all the faces it passes and join the points with a straight line.
立体の表面を通る最短の道は、面を開いて展開図にし、まっすぐ結ぶ。: For the shortest path over the surface of a solid, open the faces into a net and join the points with a straight line.
立体の表面を通る糸の長さの最小値は、面を開いた展開図の直線の長さ。三平方の定理で: The shortest string over the surface of a solid equals the length of the straight line on the net. Find it with the Pythagorean theorem.
立体の表面を通る道は、面を開いて平面にしても長さは変わらない。平面では、2点を結: A path over the surface of a solid keeps its length when you open the faces into a flat net. On a flat plane, the shortest line joining 2 points is the straight one.
立体を開いて平面にする: Open up the solid into a flat net

等積変形は、高さが変わらないときだけ使える。平行でない線の上では、頂点を動かすと: Equal-Area Slide only works when the height stays the same. On a line that isn't parallel, moving the vertex changes the height too.

What takes time on math entrance-exam problems isn't the calculation itself — it's the time you spend stuck on "how do I start?"
This workbook helps you master, one at a time, 8 viewpoints (lenses) that work across both geometry and classic word-problem types.
Each chapter shows the same problem 2 ways — "by habit (the trap)" and "through the lens" — so you can compare where the long way around happens.

範囲にまん中が入っていないときは、まん中では最大にならない。まん中に一番近いはし: If the middle isn't inside the range, the maximum doesn't happen at the middle. Check the endpoint closest to the middle.
線で折り返して、まっすぐな道にする: Reflect across a line to turn the path into a straight one

高校入試の数学は、1つの考え方では終わらず、2つの視点をつなげて解く問題が増えま:
In high-school entrance exam math, more problems can't be finished with a single idea — you solve them by linking 2 viewpoints.
This book takes the 8 viewpoints (lenses) also used in middle-school entrance exams and applies them again to coordinates, geometry and word problems.
You'll also practice the order for linking lenses, such as "reflect to find the shortest point → enclose to find the area."
